kind: photo (actual person, 11 Aug 1938, Washington) - HERO for the twist
license: Public domain. Commons tags: {{PD-Harris-Ewing}} + {{PD-US-no notice}} + {{Library of Congress-no known copyright restrictions}}. LOC rights: 'No known restrictions on publication.' (Harris & Ewing gift, 1955)
credit_line: Harris & Ewing, Library of Congress Prints & Photographs Division, LC-DIG-hec-24918 (public domain)
what_it_shows: Corrigan in his leather flying jacket on a leather sofa next to Dennis Mulligan, chief of the Bureau of Air Commerce (the official who had to discipline him). The two men point in OPPOSITE directions: Mulligan points left, Corrigan points across himself. Map on the wall behind. 10149x8069 glass-negative scan. LOC title is 'from unverified caption data'.
best_segments: Twist/'blamed his compass' beat: start tight on Corrigan's grin and pointing hand (right half), then pull back to reveal Mulligan pointing the other way. 9:16 crops: Corrigan alone x 5000-9600; both hands x 1800-9000 at reduced scale. Huge resolution, safe to push in 3-4x.

what_it_shows: Corrigan laughing into NBC microphones in his leather jacket, a man in a straw boater laughing beside him, American Airlines DC-2 fuselage behind. 10106x8121.
best_segments: Hook or result: celebrity energy. 9:16 crop centred on Corrigan x 2300-6900 (NBC mic in frame at left). Avoid implying this is Ireland: it is Washington, after his return.

best_segments: Native portrait - ideal 9:16 hook or end card. Crop x 0-5700 keeps the raised arm and face; slow push on face.

kind: photo (actual plane, Curtiss Robin NX9243, NYC dock, Aug 1938)
license: Public domain. Commons tag: {{PD-US-not renewed}}. Evidence on page: no 1938 registration under 'Acme'; no 1965/1966 renewals for Acme Newspictures or the Eugene Guard (published 10 Aug 1938, p.1). Source scan is an eBay press print (front+back).
credit_line: Acme Newspictures, 1938 (public domain, copyright not renewed), via Wikimedia Commons
what_it_shows: Corrigan's small silver high-wing cabin monoplane hanging from a crane sling against a ship's riveted hull, dock workers and onlookers below, 'JOHN T. CLARK & SON' stevedores banner. 1236x970.
best_segments: The only clear image of the actual plane: use under 'nine-year-old plane'/'ship docked'. 9:16 crop x 60-1080 at <=1.5x; slow pan nose-to-tail.

license: Not on Commons. LOC Chronicling America rights: 'The Library of Congress believes that the newspapers in Chronicling America are in the public domain or have no known copyright restrictions' (with caveat for third-party content). Headline type only - no third-party photo in this crop.
credit_line: Evening Star (Washington, D.C.), 18 July 1938, p.1. Library of Congress, Chronicling America
what_it_shows: 'CORRIGAN IN IRELAND AFTER 'SNEAK' FLIGHT IN NINE-YEAR-OLD AIRPLANE' plus the start of the 'Where Am I?' deck. Crop of the full page (evening_star_1938-07-18_p1.jpg, 2779x3888, also in folder). 1010x400.
best_segments: Hook/story slam. Full page also usable; AVOID the AP Wirephoto of Corrigan (x 420-1060, y 680-1420 on full page) and the political cartoon (top centre) as possible third-party content.

license: Not on Commons. LOC Chronicling America rights statement (same as above). Headline type only.
credit_line: Evening Star (Washington, D.C.), 5 August 1938, p.1. Library of Congress, Chronicling America
what_it_shows: Narrow column: 'GOTHAM CANYONS RING WITH ROARS TO GRINNING FLYER / Corrigan Is Tangled With Tape and Drowned in Continuous Tumult / FRENZIED WELCOME RIVALS LINDBERGH'S / Oppressive Heat Forgotten by a Million...'. Full page evening_star_1938-08-05_p1.jpg (2809x3884) also in folder. 345x640.
best_segments: Result beat ('a million people threw him a parade'). Already portrait-shaped; scale to fill, scroll down to 'a Million'.

kind: newspaper front page (parade day, Fri 5 Aug 1938)
license: Public domain. Commons tag: {{PD-US-not renewed}}. Evidence on page: 1965 and 1966 periodical renewal lists checked, no New York Post entries. WEAKER than the LOC items: originally uploaded to en.wiki as {{fairuse}} then re-tagged; source is a 2006 NY Post store product image.
credit_line: New York Post, 5 August 1938 (public domain, copyright not renewed), via Wikimedia Commons
what_it_shows: Headline printed backwards: 'HAIL WRONG WAY CORRIGAN' mirrored; 'MILLION CHEER MADLY IN WELCOME TO FLYER'; big ticker-tape crowd photo on Broadway. Date line reads FRIDAY, AUGUST 5, 1938 (Commons category wrongly says 1938-07-17). Only 400x546.
best_segments: Kicker/end gag: mirrored headline strip y 96-148. Low-res: use small with paper texture, or rebuild the mirrored headline as live type (typography is not copyrightable) and show this only as a brief insert.

what_it_shows: Corrigan in a tweed jacket scratching his head with a sheepish grin, holding an airline route map of the United States. LOC title: 'He's "Right Way" Corrigan now' [1942]. 4096x3255.
best_segments: Perfect 'blamed his compass' reaction shot, but it is 1942: don't caption it as 1938. 9:16 crop x 100-2700 (face + map).
